newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-POOR PITCH SPOILS LANCASHIRE'S TROPHY SUCCESS. [CORRECTED 08:20 GMT 8/9/]
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-POOR PITCH SPOILS LANCASHIRE'S TROPHY SUCCESS. [CORRECTED 08:20 GMT 8/9/]

text.p: Essex made just 57, the lowest total ever in a Lord's final, as Lancashire (Corrects from Derbyshire) won the Natwest Trophy by 129 runs on Saturday.
Glen Chapple took six for 18 but the real destroyer was a controversial Lord's pitch, a seaming surface which also produced increasingly inconsistent bounce.
Not even Graham Gooch, seventh out for 10 to a shooter from Jason Gallian, could make and headway as Essex's capitulation took only 27.2 overs.
Besides Chapple, Lancashire had other heroes in Peter Martin, who took three for 17, and batsman John Crawley, who made 66 as they scored 186 and repeated their cup double triumph of 1990.

But though the shortest September final in the 34-year history of the event will be remembered more for the harshness of the conditions than for individual performances, Chapple produced some magnificent deliveries in a spell of 6.2 overs.
The ball which removed Robert Rollins for a golden duck would have beaten almost anybody.

Gooch's struggle through 86 minutes and 55 balls, in which he hit just one four, summed up the difficulty while Essex will also point to Ronnie Irani's crucial downfall to a delivery which crept wickedly to hit off stump barely a third of the way up.
When Gooch was seventh out at 33 and Mark Ilott was adjudged lbw to the rampant Chapple, Essex were in danger _ at 34 for eight _ of failing to go past the lowest score in the competition.
But two lusty fours from Ashley Cowan spared them the embarrassment of falling short of the 39 Ireland compiled against Sussex at Hove in 1994.
And Middlesex's 41, ironically against Essex in 1972, also still stands as the lowest by a county side.
It was the biggest winning margin in a September final for 31 years and means Lancashire have now won the domestic game's premier one-day trophy six times, more than any other county.
Ball held sway over bat from the start, England captain Mike Atherton being clean bowled for four by a late inswinger from the impressive Ilott.
And all-rounder Irani, pressing for a winter tour place, looked like he was delivering a significant spell when he reduced Lancashire to 88 for four in a 12-over stint of three for 25.
Crawley, however, stood firm to make sure Lancashire, put in when they would have gone against tradition and batted anyway, reached a defendable score.
Mike Watkinson, Warren Hegg and Ian Austin all made valuable contributions but no-one, not even the Lancashire bowlers, could have expected to defend 186 with quite so much ease.

Gooch, in what may be his last appearance at Lord's, did leave with one good memory - the moment he flung his 43-year old frame down to his right at slip to hold the blinding catch which ended Graham Lloyd's brief innings.
In the end, though, Essex badly missed their overseas star, Stuart Law, still in Sri Lanka with Australia, while Lancashire had enough firepower to do without their South African, Steve Elworthy.
